title: Role-token matrix and revocation contract

trigger_classes.attempt-end: The attempt that holds a credential issued for that single attempt ends, in any outcome. Never a trigger of a standing credential that the Gitea site administrator issues (decision 0007, amendment 1, point 3).
trigger_classes.suspected-exposure: The credential may have been read or used outside its role.
trigger_classes.definition-revocation: The agent or Skill definition the attempt runs is revoked.
trigger_classes.policy-revision: A policy revision changes what the role may hold.

in_flight: The dispatcher stops or contains the attempts holding the credential through op-as-runtime-stop and records them as exposed.
Gitea fails closed at the credential's next authenticated call.
CI jobs holding it are cancelled.
evidence: A Gitea audit record, where audit logging is enabled (it is off by default).
A revocation receipt in the integration store: never the credential itself.
revocation_contract.effects_store_exception: A revocation that is itself an executor effect leaves its receipt in the effects store (decision 0004, point 1).
revocation_contract.privileged_rotation: Rotating a privileged credential (Owner, admin, executor or management class) is a consequential external effect: an Owner-only manifest applied by the executor in the target, or an Owner act recorded in the bootstrap log during bootstrap.

capabilities.name: Merge a code PR into a protected integration branch
capabilities.description: Merging a code pull request into a protected integration branch under the branch rules (required checks and independent review). Distinct from the Owner-only merge of an operation manifest on the authorization branch.

delegation.to: permitted automation only, by repository policy; never an agent or CI role

capabilities.name: Read repositories
capabilities.description: Read the repositories in scope, their pull requests and diffs.

capabilities.name: Push a proposal branch
capabilities.description: Push `work/*` proposal branches; never a protected ref.

capabilities.name: Open a pull request
capabilities.description: Open a pull request from a proposal branch.

capabilities.name: Submit a review
capabilities.description: Submit a review as evidence; a review never merges.

capabilities.name: Report CI statuses and artifacts
capabilities.description: Report commit statuses and upload artifacts for the job's own run, within the job token's repository context.
capabilities.notes: Granted to no role since Q-02.1: the validation job reports nothing; the runner streams its log and the trusted lane posts the status (decision 0016, Proposed, section 5.3).

capabilities.name: Push to a protected ref
capabilities.description: Push, force-push or API-merge directly to a protected ref, bypassing the merge rules. No role is granted it: protected refs change only through protected merges.

capabilities.name: Change Work status
capabilities.description: Change a Work item's status. Backlog status belongs to the deterministic coordinator, which the inventory does not name yet; no role here is granted it.

roles.name: The Owner

realization.mechanism: A separate Gitea Owner account (aieh-owner), the only identity on the authorization branch's merge allowlist, never signed in to and holding no token; its credential is held by the authorization recorder, its sole custodian, which merges as it on a recorded Owner decision; never a personal access token in any agent or CI context.
realization.notes: Shown at S-01.2.2: aieh-owner is the only merge-allowlist identity of every protected-branch rule of the fixture, and it holds no access token (finalize-credentials). Shown live in P-04.2's exercise (2026-11-12; decision 0012): on the Owner's authorization of OA-14 the authorization recorder merged one exact operation manifest into the fixture's protected main as aieh-owner by basic authentication (merge 75e89b28143464949c24bd46433a5d9f2197b0d0, receipt confirmed), and aieh-owner held zero tokens after the merge; the custody inspection found aieh-owner's password in no file of the managed root, the checkout or the run directory and not in the main session's process environment. No job environment existed: its absence from agent attempts is S-03.3's and from CI jobs Q-02.2.2's (evidence/P-04.2-authorization-recorder.md, section 17). This row covers the Gitea Owner account only; the custody of the Owner's own credentials (cred-owner-github, cred-owner-provider-login) is not inspected (fd-owner-credential-custody). The authorization repository (aieh-authorization/authorizations) exists since Owner act OA-30 (2026-11-13; plan leaf E-05.7) with no merge on it yet (fd-owner-authorization-record).

realization.mechanism: Code merges into protected integration branches under the D-01.2 branch rules.
realization.notes: Not exercised at S-01.2.2: no Owner merge was performed (the Owner credential is not used by tests); the D-01.2 branch rules are not applied yet.

issuance.delivery: Given interactively on the secure desktop for one specifically authorized elevated operation, which an agent may initiate (decision 0004, Owner clarification 4); never stored.

Created on the Gitea instance as an Owner act (F-06.1); its password is harness-held: set by credential finalization under the Owner's approval of 2026-11-07 into the credential provider entry "AIEH Gitea owner", which only the authorization recorder, its custodian, reads (P-04.2; decision 0012). The Owner never signs in to Gitea (Owner directive of 2026-11-07).

A separate Owner session credential to the Owner-host/Integration process, not shaped like an Agent Server key (decision 0013, point 5); issued only by an Owner act. Which leaf builds it is unsettled (fd-owner-ui-session-plan-silence).

Issued per Owner session by the dispatcher from the outer server's runtime-credentials route, bounded to that conversation and the Owner's session, and handed to the Owner UI with a dispatcher-owned local forward bound to host 127.0.0.1 (decision 0013, points 2 and 3); never stored in a record, log or repository. The Owner UI never holds the management key.

revocation.method: It lapses after its one operation; the Owner withholds or withdraws consent.
Disable the account or reset its password and sessions on the Gitea instance, as an Owner act.
Not defined until a leaf builds the Owner's UI session to the Integration process (plan silence); the Owner ends the session.

It ends with the Owner's session or the conversation's container, whichever ends first: the dispatcher closes the local forward, and stopping the runtime or deleting the conversation ends the credential (op-as-runtime-stop). On suspected exposure the dispatcher stops the conversation's runtime.

roles.target: Owner-only operations, the Gitea Owner account on the authorization branch's merge allowlist only, UAC consent for specifically authorized elevated acts, public-repository push, and code merges into protected integration branches. Never a personal access token in any agent or CI context.

bootstrap.note: The Owner directs the work and approves privileged host acts by UAC consent. The Gitea Owner account aieh-owner exists (F-06.1); its credential is harness-held (Owner directive of 2026-11-07: the Owner never signs in to Gitea), and the authorization recorder (P-04.2) is its sole custodian, merging as it only on a recorded Owner decision; it is the only merge-allowlist identity of the S-01.2.2 fixture; public pushes run from the Owner's account.

roles.name: The Owner's host account

issuance.delivery: Generated per instance at create by the system ssh-keygen into the per-instance directory; recreate issues a new one.
The Owner's own account at the provider; custody not inspected.
The Owner's own coding-assistant login; never a role token.

revocation.method: Guest destroy removes it and recreate issues a new one.
Revoked and reissued at the provider by the Owner.
Signed out or revoked at the provider by the Owner.

roles.target: The Owner's interactive host account: guest lifecycle, exec, exchange, session-key export and provisioning fetch. It holds no executor or service identity, and no executor credential is stored in its credential store.

bootstrap.note: Host tooling under this account performs every operation of this row, and the host-side bootstrap agents share the account (fd-bootstrap-shared-identity).

roles.name: Gitea site administrator

realization.mechanism: The Gitea site-administrator account; branch protection with the admin force-merge override disabled, so the administrator obeys the branch rules.
realization.notes: Verified at S-01.2.2: the fixture's default-branch rule carries block_admin_merge_override; the site administrator's merge and force-merge of a proposal PR both answered 405 "User not allowed to merge PR", and the default branch did not change.

realization.mechanism: Issues Gitea identities, bot accounts and their tokens, protection rules and runner registration secrets; never exposed to agents or CI.
realization.notes: Partly shown at S-01.2.2: the protection rules, organization, repository and collaborators were issued by the site administrator through the API (basic authentication, password in memory, no token); the bot accounts and tokens through Gitea's CLI by the Owner's host account; the administrator can list and revoke another account's token (200, 204, then 401). No runner registration secret exists (fd-ci-runner-unpinned). The credential is read only by credential finalization and the fixture administration. Re-pointed to Q-02.2.1 by the plan reconciliation of 2026-11-08 (evidence/plan-reconciliation-2026-11-08.md): what remains unverified is the runner registration secret, which the runner provisioning creates.

issuance.delivery: Created by F-06.1 with Gitea's CLI; its final password is generated and set by task gitea:finalize-credentials and held by the harness in the credential provider (Owner directive of 2026-11-07); read only by credential finalization and the fixture administration.

revocation.method: Rotated by the Owner on the Gitea instance: a consequential external effect.

roles.target: Site administration of Gitea under the branch rules; issues Gitea identities, bot accounts, protection rules and runner registration secrets. Never exposed to agents or CI.

bootstrap.note: Gitea 28.3.0 runs on host loopback (F-06.1). aieh-site-admin holds a harness-held password set by task gitea:finalize-credentials (Owner directive of 2026-11-07: no Owner sign-in), which also revoked its leftover tokens. Gitea administration during bootstrap is performed by the Owner's host account: identities, bots and tokens through Gitea's CLI, the fixture as the site administrator through the API.

roles.name: Planning agent

realization.mechanism: A dedicated, non-administrator Gitea bot account and token.
realization.notes: Verified at S-01.2.2: aieh-bot-planner, a restricted, non-administrator Gitea Bot account without a password; token scope write:repository only; every Owner, administrator, user and token operation probed was refused, and it pushed work/authz-planner and opened a PR.

realization.mechanism: Planning-artefact-only writes, pending the layout: a repository-level permission if planning artefacts get their own repository, or a required scoped-workflow check on PR paths if they are co-located.
realization.notes: Unknown at S-01.2.2: Gitea 28.3.0 token scopes are categorical and no path-level scope exists; pending the planning-artefact layout (decision 0007, point 2). Deferred by the plan reconciliation of 2026-11-08 (evidence/plan-reconciliation-2026-11-08.md) (authority: the Overseer; no leaf dispatches a planner in a guest, the planner runs on the Owner's headless channel, P-01.2; reconsider when a planner role is dispatched in a guest, A-01.x or E-03.x). verify_at keeps S-01.2.2, the leaf that recorded it, because no plan leaf owns it.

issuance.delivery: Used per attempt by the dispatcher in the attempt environment only: the dispatcher's attempt context, never the conversation container (decision 0013, point 7; decision 0007 points 4 and 5, amendment 1). The standing token is obtained only for a confirmed attempt of the mapped role, held in memory for the bounded operation and released when it ends; releasing the in-memory reference is not Gitea revocation. Gitea 28.3.0 cannot bound a token to an attempt (no token lifetime) and gives the dispatcher no replacement mechanism, so the token is issued, rotated and revoked only by the site administrator's lifecycle (gitea_roles.py provision, rotate, retire). Never in an image, seed, repository, log or record (fingerprints only). No stage is mapped to the planner yet (integrations/dispatch/attempt_tokens.py maps implement and review).
Passed by the Agent Server's Docker runtime as environment values into the conversation container.

Issued per attempt by the inference broker alone (decision 0007 point 4) on its control listener to the dispatcher, before the create: bound to the attempt's reserved conversation, one API family, a model list and an expiry (no request or token budget: decision 0015 amendment 2), returned once and kept by the broker as its digest only. The dispatcher places it in the create request (an ACP agent: the create's secrets under the pinned registry's api_key_env_var, with the endpoint under base_url_env_var; a native agent: the LLM settings' api_key), so the attempt's agent can read it by design (decision 0015 sections 3.2 and 3.3, amendment 1 point 2). It is issued by the broker and is not a role token: no role token is ever sent to the broker and no provider credential is ever a role token. Records carry its fingerprint only.

revocation.method: Three lifecycles (decision 0007 points 4 and 5, amendment 1; E-01.3.3, the Owner's correction of 2026-11-11). (1) The standing token is rotated and revoked only by the site administrator's lifecycle, on defined security and lifecycle triggers and never on routine attempt completion, so attempt end is not among its triggers: gitea_roles.py rotate (revokes through DELETE /api/v1/token, proves the next call answers 401, re-issues with Gitea's CLI and replaces the entry; it resumes over a token Gitea already refuses) and retire; the site administrator can also list and delete another account's token, which then answers 401 (observed at S-01.2.2), or disable the bot account. (2) At attempt end the dispatcher only releases its in-memory reference, which is not Gitea revocation; a token Gitea refuses is not delivered (ROLE_TOKEN_REJECTED) until the administrative lifecycle replaces it. (3) The per-attempt inference token is a separate credential, revoked at attempt end (decision 0015). Residual, recorded as a limit: concurrent attempts of one role share one standing token, and re-issue is an administration act between attempts, because Gitea 28.3.0 has no token lifetime and gives the dispatcher no replacement mechanism (the dispatcher is granted no issuance). Disclosed same-account limit: during bootstrap the Owner's account can read the standing token in its Credential Manager (decision 0013 point 6).
They end with their container: stopping the runtime or deleting the conversation removes them.

The dispatcher asks the broker's control listener to revoke the grant by its fingerprint at attempt end and on any other trigger, and the broker revokes it itself at expiry; revocation is immediate (the next request answers 401) and leaves a receipt (fingerprint, attempt, trigger, revoker) in the integration store, never in the effects store (decision 0015 section 3.3).

roles.target: Its own Gitea bot identity and token: read the repositories in scope, push `work/*` proposal branches and open PRs whose writes are planning artefacts only.

bootstrap.note: Its Gitea bot account and token exist (S-01.2.2), in the Owner account's Credential Manager pending the dispatcher; no agent workload has run or held the token (decision 0003, C6).

realization.notes: Failed in part at S-01.2.2. roles.name: CI job executing pull-request code

realization.mechanism: The Gitea Actions job token, permissionless and inert: restricted mode and an all-none ceiling at the governance owner and repository, permissions: {} in the workflow, no cross-repository grant, no public repository, and no network path from the job (decision 0016, Proposed, section 5).
realization.notes: Unknown at S-01.2.2: no CI runner is selected or pinned and Gitea Actions is off (fd-ci-runner-unpinned). Re-pointed to Q-02.3.1, which sets the job-token maxima, by the plan reconciliation of 2026-11-08 (evidence/plan-reconciliation-2026-11-08.md). Q-02.1 (2026-11-10): Gitea 28.3.0 has the ceilings at source (G4 of policy/ci-token-secret-policy.json); Q-02.3.1 applies and reads them back.

realization.mechanism: A disposable container or VM on a dedicated runner host: no host-mode execution, host Docker socket, user home, Owner credential or release, signing or deployment secret.
realization.notes: Unknown at S-01.2.2: no CI runner is selected or pinned and Gitea Actions is off (fd-ci-runner-unpinned). Re-pointed to Q-02.2.2, which provisions and inspects the disposable CI job, by the plan reconciliation of 2026-11-08 (evidence/plan-reconciliation-2026-11-08.md).

realization.mechanism: The runner containment profile carries the job constraints of S-01.3.2: no engine socket or engine TCP endpoint reachable from a job; no management key, Owner, admin or bot token in its environment or readable filesystem; no privileged mode, added capability, device or host namespace; no host-path mount beyond the scoped workspace.
realization.notes: Declared at S-01.3.2 (provisioning.agent_server.jobs.ci), not verified: no CI runner exists. The profile is Q-02.2.1; Q-02.2.2 proves it and Q-02.3.2 attempts the engine socket from a hostile job.

issuance.delivery: Minted by Gitea Actions for one task and placed by the runner in the job environment; its effective permission is none on the governance repository and every other private repository (policy/ci-token-secret-policy.json); it is inert and never relied on.
Minted by Gitea per task in the task context (gitea_runtime_token); treated as present in the job environment (act_runner, verified at Q-02.2.1); inert and never relied on.

revocation.method: It ends with its task; on suspected exposure the dispatcher cancels the run and recreates the CI guest.
It ends with its task at the artifact routes and expires with the JWT; on suspected exposure the dispatcher cancels the run and recreates the CI guest.

roles.target: The governance workflow's job: no network path, no secret, and two inert task tokens; it reports nothing (the runner streams its log and the trusted lane posts the status).

bootstrap.note: No CI runner is selected or pinned, and no CI job has run.

roles.name: CI runner service

realization.mechanism: The runner's registration secret passes through the CI guest once, in memory, and is reset after registration; the runner's persistent token stays on the CI guest, root-owned outside every mount and unreachable from the job filesystem.
realization.notes: Unknown at S-01.2.2: no CI runner is selected or pinned (fd-ci-runner-unpinned). Re-pointed to Q-02.3.2, whose hostile job attempts secret reads, by the plan reconciliation of 2026-11-08 (evidence/plan-reconciliation-2026-11-08.md).

issuance.delivery: Reset and read by the host-side Gitea-administration command, carried once in the dispatcher's memory over the management channel to the CI guest's register step, and reset again after registration; never at rest.
Issued by Gitea to the runner at registration; kept root-owned on the CI guest.

revocation.method: Reset by the Gitea-administration command after every registration and on any trigger; the reset is the revocation.

Always at CI-guest destroy: the Gitea-administration command deletes the runner record (owner-only route) and Gitea refuses the token at its next poll; an ephemeral runner is deleted by Gitea when its task ends.

roles.target: The runner token on the CI guest, unreachable from jobs; registration to the governance repository only.

realization.mechanism: The sole holder of the Agent Server session key, on the trusted side; admission to the create and admin routes is limited to its identity and network (S-01.3.1).
realization.notes: Not realized at S-01.3.1: no dispatcher exists, and during bootstrap the Owner's account holds the key through the operator login. The admission half is verified (next row); sole custody of the key is decided with the dispatcher (E-01.2.x). Re-pointed to E-01.3.3 by the plan reconciliation of 2026-11-08 (evidence/plan-reconciliation-2026-11-08.md): the dispatcher identity becomes the sole reader of the management key there. E-01.3.3 (2026-11-11, the bootstrap reading of decision 0013 point 1, the Overseer's ruling F-2): the dispatcher principal is the Owner's account acting through the dispatch module (integrations/dispatch/guest_transport.py) over tools/guest.py's GuestApi as the guest login agent, which reads the key from its root:agent 0440 file in the guest only; the cut-over is the code path (op-as-* on Work only through the dispatch module); the host copy is disclosed under point 6; separating an operator login from the dispatcher's guest login waits for the dispatcher's own host identity (no leaf; routed to the Owner). Built offline; not yet verified live (the custody probe is prepared, unrun).

realization.mechanism: Admission to the Agent Server's management API by key and by network: every key-gated route refuses a missing or wrong key (HTTP 401, WebSocket close 4001 or handshake 403); the server does not start without a valid key; the listener is on the guest loopback only and no conversation container reaches it, the guest itself or another container (container guard, icc off). The per-route allowlist of the dispatcher (routes.json) is policy for the dispatcher, not a server control.
realization.notes: Verified live on a disposable provisioned guest (guest.py admission-probe, before and after a guest restart): all 193 routes of the inventory, and connections from two conversation containers to every guest address.

realization.mechanism: Custodian of the standing bot credentials, which stay on the trusted host in the OS credential provider: for a confirmed attempt it borrows only the stage's mapped credential into its own in-memory attempt context and releases it when the operation ends, which is not Gitea revocation; a standing credential never enters a guest, an agent environment, a container, a conversation, a conversation record or the UI; records carry fingerprints only; it issues, rotates and revokes no standing credential (decision 0007 points 4 and 5, amendment 1).
realization.notes: Not verified at S-01.2.2: no dispatcher exists. Bootstrap custody observed instead: the Credential Manager entries "AIEH Gitea bot <role>" of the Owner's account, written by owner-os-account; records carry fingerprints only. Refined by decision 0013, point 7 (S-01.4): the attempt environment is the dispatcher's attempt context, never the conversation container; untrusted code has no network path to Gitea, proposals leave by exchange and the dispatcher pushes as the bot identity it holds custody of. Re-pointed to E-01.3.3 by the plan reconciliation of 2026-11-08 (evidence/plan-reconciliation-2026-11-08.md): per-attempt role-token delivery and rotation are built and proved there. E-01.3.3 (2026-11-11, offline, not yet verified live): integrations/dispatch/attempt_tokens.py delivers each stage's standing token per confirmed attempt into the dispatcher's attempt context and releases the in-memory reference at its end, which is not Gitea revocation; per-attempt rotation is not done: the standing token is rotated and revoked only by the site administrator's lifecycle (gitea_roles.py rotate, retire) on defined triggers (the Owner's correction of 2026-11-11; decision 0007 point 4). Restated on 2026-11-11 under decision 0007 amendment 1 (OA-20); the superseded mechanism read "delivers each agent role token per attempt into the attempt environment only".

realization.mechanism: The sole network path to the management API: the dispatcher's management calls and the Owner UI's conversation connections ride the qualified management channel (the loopback-bound SSH forward with the per-instance key); no browser, UI process, Integration process or agent holds the management key, and no QEMU hostfwd of the management listener exists (decision 0013, points 1 and 3).
realization.notes: Decided at S-01.4 (decision 0013, Proposed); not realized: no dispatcher exists. The network half that exists today is in the matrix (policy/network-matrix.json): the listener is on the guest's loopback only, no host forward of it exists and no container reaches it.

issuance.delivery: Generated in the guest at provisioning; read by the operator login from its root:agent 0440 file during bootstrap (S-01.3.1); it is to reach only the dispatcher over a trusted channel (E-01.2.x). Records carry fingerprints only. During bootstrap (decision 0013 point 1, E-01.3.3) the dispatcher is the Owner's account through the dispatch module over GuestApi as agent: the key is read in the guest only, never on a command line or in the host process.

revocation.method: Only guest recreate and provision revokes it, which ends every conversation.

roles.target: Sole holder of the Agent Server session key; the Agent Server management operations; custodian and per-attempt deliverer of the standing bot credentials. It writes no effect receipt.

bootstrap.note: No dispatcher exists. The Owner's account performs conversation create and runtime control through the operator login (see the sunset map).

roles.name: Owner authorization recorder

realization.mechanism: The protection auditor aieh-bot-protection-audit (Owner decision OA-16): a restricted Gitea Bot without a password, repository-administrator collaborator of the admitted repository only, whose token of scope exactly read:repository (cred-gitea-protection-audit) the recorder's protection check (integrations/gitea/protection_check.py) alone reads, for the last read before each merge and the first after it; every write by that token is refused by its scope.
realization.notes: Built and tested at P-04.2 against fake Gitea servers (evidence/P-04.2-protection-verifier.md). Verified live on 2026-11-12, each an Owner act (evidence/bootstrap-log.md, Decisions): the auditor provisioned (OA-16 Act A) and the fixture's total declaration applied (Act B: verified); the negative tests (Act C: the auditor reads the rules; every write by its token, git pushes included, refused 403 by its scope; aieh-authz-fixture/escape-probe's rules not readable); the qualification (Act D: five injected drifts, each detected and its restoration verified); and the check answering verified before and after the recorder's one live merge (evidence/P-04.2-authorization-recorder.md, section 17).

issuance.delivery: Provisioned on 2026-11-12 (Owner decision OA-16, Act A): minted by the site administrator through Gitea's CLI (gitea_roles.py provision: generate-access-token --raw, scope read:repository) for the restricted Bot aieh-bot-protection-audit, a repository-administrator collaborator of the admitted repository only, and written by the credential provider into the entry "AIEH Gitea bot protection-audit"; the recorder's protection check reads it by name, into memory, for one check. Never in an agent context, a guest, a log or a record (fingerprints only).

revocation.method: gitea_roles.py rotate protection-audit (revoke through DELETE /api/v1/token, prove the next call is refused, mint and store a new one) or retire protection-audit (revoke, then delete the entry), each with its integration-store receipt; the site administrator can also list and delete the bot's tokens or disable the account. A revoked or missing token makes the protection check answer unverified, so the recorder merges nothing.

roles.target: Custodian of cred-gitea-owner-account, the delegated performer of op-protected-merge, whose principal stays the Owner: on a recorded Owner decision it merges one exact operation manifest into the protected authorization branch as aieh-owner (Do: merge with head_commit_id; merge commits only; the decision trailers; a write-ahead receipt in the integration store), by HTTP basic authentication with the password read from the credential provider into memory for each command. It never mints or sends a token and never uses sudo, force_merge or auto-merge; it refuses an entry naming another account or holding a token, and an aieh-owner that is an administrator or holds a token. It has no agent-callable or MCP surface and runs only in the main session on an Owner decision (decision 0012). Its protection check (Owner decision OA-16; decision 0012 point 6) is the last read before each merge and the first after it: as aieh-bot-protection-audit, a restricted Gitea Bot with repository-administrator collaboration on the repositories it audits only (the fixture and, since Owner act OA-30, the authorization repository) and a token of scope exactly read:repository (cred-gitea-protection-audit, whose custodian it is), it reads every protection rule (34 fields each), the exact rule set and the effective rule, the merge settings, the collaborators with their permissions, the teams and the deploy keys, and refuses the merge on drift or on anything it cannot verify (integrations/gitea/protection_check.py). Verified at P-04.2's live qualification (OA-16 Acts C and D, 2026-11-12): the auditor reads the rules and every write by its token is refused.

bootstrap.note: Built at P-04.2 (task owner:authorize); on a real Gitea it has merged once, on the S-01.2.2 fixture on the Owner's authorization of OA-14 (2026-11-12), run as a process of the Owner's account in the main session. During bootstrap it runs as a process of the Owner's account, which the host-side bootstrap agents share (fd-bootstrap-shared-identity; decision 0010). Its protection check reads as the protection auditor, provisioned and qualified live on 2026-11-12 (OA-16 Acts A to D).
